clue.text: Loss of power, with liberal disappearing in retreat

indicators.note: something disappearing vanishes from view, so that piece is taken away

parts.note: a blackout is a failure of the electricity supply
L is the standard abbreviation for liberal

explanation.surface: A political story: the liberals vanish from power as their side falls back.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the L out of BLACKOUT to leave BACKOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To back out of something is to withdraw from it, a verb synonym of retreat.

clue.text: Shortening overtime to catch a pop-up? In Florida, it might lead to confusion

definitions.text: In Florida, it might lead to confusion

indicators.note: to catch something is to take hold of it, so the outer pair of words closes round the next one

parts.note: butter is a fat used as shortening in baking
in baseball a pop-up is a ball hit high in the air
OT is the usual abbreviation for overtime

explanation.surface: A baseball game goes into extra innings, cut short when a fielder catches a high hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition recalls the 2000 US presidential election, when Palm Beach County's confusing ballot design misled voters.
explanation.definitionFit: The butterfly ballot's staggered two-page layout made Florida voters pick candidates they never intended, so it is a design blamed for confusion.

clue.text: Hear, touch or taste money

indicators.note: hearing a word means attending to its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: touch and taste are two of the five senses

explanation.surface: A list of ways to experience cash: listening, feeling or tasting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' looks like a third sense listed with touch and taste, but it is the signal to listen.
explanation.definitionFit: Cents are the hundredth parts of a dollar, small coins, hence money.

clue.text: I mean to eat bananas individually

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: these ten letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone planning to eat their bananas singly rather than by the bunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like the food being eaten; it is an adjective meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things one at a time means handling each separately, the sense of individually.

clue.text: Henry and Elizabeth Stroud, horsing around

indicators.note: horsing around is fooling about, so the letters are jumbled playfully

parts.note: these six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A married couple called Henry and Elizabeth Stroud are larking about, perhaps on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry and Elizabeth look like the Strouds' first names, but they are the kings and queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VII, Henry VIII and Elizabeth I were monarchs of the Tudor royal house of England.

clue.text: Rural ailment afflicting infants at a New England school?

parts.note: BU is Boston University, in Massachusetts
colic is the bouts of crying and stomach pain common in babies

explanation.surface: Some countryside illness of babies has broken out at a college in New England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rural ailment' reads as one phrase, but Rural alone is the definition; the ailment is the babies' complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucolic is a literary adjective for things of the countryside and pastoral life.

clue.text: Every fortnight, said farewell in a half-hearted manner

indicators.note: said means spoken aloud, so the words count by their sound

parts.note: bye is a casual goodbye
doing something weakly is doing it without conviction

explanation.surface: Someone says a feeble goodbye on a fortnightly visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' looks like the verb for the goodbye, but it signals the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Biweekly can mean once every two weeks, and a fortnight is a period of two weeks.

clue.text: Rope, using ____ for a new beginning, becomes cope or dope

indicators.note: the beginning is the opening letter of a word, the only part that changes

parts.note: the opening letter of cope
taken as written
the opening letter of dope

explanation.surface: A word puzzle: replace one letter of rope and it turns into other words.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank is filled by the letters C or D, and that phrase run together is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord is a thin rope or thick string.

clue.text: Middle Eastern variety of orange is held up over the end of a fork

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding something up raises it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a navel orange is a seedless variety
a tine is one of the prongs at the end of a fork

explanation.surface: A type of orange from the Middle East is lifted on the prongs of a fork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' means placed above, as in a down clue the first part sits on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Levantine describes the Levant, the eastern Mediterranean lands such as Lebanon and Syria.

clue.text: Writer Ford (and others) covering host with those making a selection

parts.note: a Ford is a car, and the others make it plural
a cover lies on what it covers
MC, master of ceremonies, is a show's host
to cull is to pick out from a group

explanation.surface: Writer Richard Ford and his peers judging a panel that chooses prizewinners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer Ford' reads as one name, the novelist Richard Ford, but Writer stands alone and Ford is the car maker. Carson McCullers wrote The Heart Is a Lonely Hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: Carson McCullers was an American novelist of the Southern Gothic school, so an example of a writer.

clue.text: For example, the past 10 heads of 7-Eleven

parts.note: the number written as a word

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so each of the two numbers gives only its first

parts.note: seven and eleven, each cut to its first letter

explanation.surface: A trivia question about the last ten managers of the 7-Eleven convenience store chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 7-Eleven looks like the shop's name, but it is read as the two numbers seven and eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: The past is one grammatical tense of a verb, alongside present and future, so it is an example.

clue.text: Motorist has to keep closer to the ocean

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a motorist is someone who drives a car
to have something is to own it

explanation.surface: A driver must stay nearer the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motorist' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the outer word that holds the possession.
explanation.definitionFit: Rivers flow to the sea, so a point further downstream along one lies nearer the ocean.

clue.text: Nerd to bully: "Start to expect a devious strategy"

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, and only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of expect

indicators.note: something devious is twisted and indirect, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the jumbled letters
taken as written, part of the jumbled letters

explanation.surface: A nerd warns a bully to expect some cunning plan in return.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation looks like the nerd's words, but 'Nerd to bully' is the definition: what a nerd is from the bully's point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: A bully picks on whoever is easiest to pick on, and the stereotyped nerd is that obvious victim.

clue.text: Sound opinion involving a command that is unfortunately not available in real life

definitions.text: a command that is unfortunately not available in real life

indicators.note: involving means containing, so the run of letters sits inside the neighbouring words

parts.note: the letters straddle the break between the two words

explanation.surface: A sensible view about a computer command that real life sadly lacks.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across 'soUND Opinion'. The definition is a wry nod to the editing command that reverses one's last action.
explanation.definitionFit: Software lets you reverse a mistake with a single keystroke; life offers no such reversal of past actions.

clue.text: Handle check to underwrite second-rate accommodations

parts.note: B grade is second-rate, below A
rooms are lodgings
a tick is a check mark

explanation.surface: Someone has to take care of a cheque guaranteeing payment for cheap lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underwrite' means write beneath: in a down clue the check mark goes below the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A broomstick is the long handle of a broom.

clue.text: Loses consciousness in fast, surprisingly

indicators.note: a surprising result is an unexpected one, hinting the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: these six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone keeling over unexpectedly while fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: To faint is to pass out, a direct synonym for losing consciousness briefly.

clue.text: Silence? No, misbehaving!

indicators.note: misbehaving means acting up, so the preceding words are disorderly

parts.note: these nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A teacher demands quiet from a class that answers back.
explanation.walkthrough: The last word serves twice: it is the definition and the anagram signal, which is why the whole clue reads as a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolence is rude, disrespectful behaviour, so misbehaving in a cheeky way.

clue.text: For Arabs, the axiom is unselfishness

parts.note: al is the Arabic definite article, as in Al-Jazeera
a truism is a self-evident truth, like an axiom

explanation.surface: A claim that, among Arabs, selflessness is a guiding principle.
explanation.definitionFit: Altruism is concern for the welfare of others, the virtue of not putting oneself first.

clue.text: Greek sporting inane hat

indicators.note: sporting can mean playful, so the letters romp into a new arrangement

parts.note: these eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A Greek man wearing a silly hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporting' reads as wearing, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An Athenian is a citizen of Athens, the Greek capital, so a Greek.

clue.text: Hey, a Jew in a national park!

parts.note: yo is a slangy greeting, like hey
Jews are a Semitic people

explanation.surface: Someone calls out to a Jewish friend spotted on a camping trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Yosemite in California is one of the best-known parks in the US national park system.

clue.text: Repeat what I say: "Moving in pairs, shift from front to back." That's what girls used to be taught

definitions.note: a clause standing for the thing taught, read with the link 'That's what' before it

indicators.text: Moving in pairs, shift from front to back
indicators.note: the letters move two at a time, with the leading couple carried round to the rear

parts.note: to echo is to repeat back
what I would say referring to myself

explanation.surface: A dance or etiquette teacher drilling a class of girls who must copy her instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests dance steps, but the pairs are pairs of letters. Home ec, short for home economics, was cooking and sewing taught at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Home economics, cooking and sewing, was once a school subject taught mainly to girls.

clue.text: Cruelly poke at Midwestern capital

indicators.note: doing something cruelly is roughing it up, so the letters are knocked about

parts.note: these six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a Midwestern state capital unkindly.
explanation.definitionFit: Topeka is the state capital of Kansas, in the American Midwest.

clue.text: Within the law: to sacrifice limb for a friend

indicators.note: sacrificing something means giving it up, so a part is lost

parts.note: acting legally is acting within the law
a leg is a limb

explanation.surface: A grim question about whether the law permits losing an arm or leg for a mate.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove LEG from the front of LEGALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is someone on your side, a partner or supporter, so a friend.

clue.text: First off, quakes spilled fuel — sorry

indicators.note: something spilled is scattered about, so the letters land in a new order
the first letter is taken off, so the word loses its opening

parts.note: tremors are small earthquakes
these four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An apology after earthquakes cause a fuel spill.
explanation.walkthrough: TREMORS loses its T, then the jumbled fuel follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorseful means feeling regret for a wrong done, which is what being sorry is.

clue.text: Oddball criticism at outset of evaluation

parts.note: flak is hostile criticism

indicators.note: the outset is the beginning, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of evaluation

explanation.surface: An eccentric is criticised at the start of a performance review.
explanation.definitionFit: A flake is informal for an eccentric or unreliable person, a crank.

clue.text: Resistance units initially on Her Majesty's service

indicators.note: initially points to the first letters of the words that follow

parts.note: the first letters of on, Her, Majesty's and service

explanation.surface: Fighters in a resistance movement work as agents of the British Crown.
explanation.walkthrough: OHMS, On Her Majesty's Service, was printed on British official mail and gave a James Bond title.
explanation.definitionFit: The ohm is the SI unit of electrical resistance.

clue.text: Large bats hunt mice when hunger is apt to strike

definitions.text: when hunger is apt to strike

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, so the following letters go haywire

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes
these eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Big bats go out hunting mice when they get hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' reads as the animals that hunt, but it is an adjective meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is the usual time people start wanting a meal, so a cryptic description of the noon meal hour.

clue.text: Overcome with anger, how a critic would describe his work

parts.note: a critic speaking of himself says I
a critic's work is to rate and grade things

explanation.surface: A furious critic explains what his job is.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as I RATE: a critic rates things for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means angry, furious, so someone overcome by rage is irate.

clue.text: Charge levied at whistleblower by despicable senator

indicators.note: a despicable figure is crooked, so the following word is bent out of shape

parts.note: these seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A contemptible politician accuses a whistleblower of a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Leakers of state secrets are often accused of betraying their country, the crime of treason.

clue.text: Socks financial institution, starting late with rents

indicators.note: starting late means missing the beginning, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a bank is a financial institution
to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: A bank punches its tenants, opening late and collecting rents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Socks' reads as a verb, to punch, but it is the plural noun for footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Anklets are short socks reaching just to the ankle.
